correctness.rationale: For all n>=3 and theta>-1/2, reconstruct the partition recursion and Lagrange coefficient formula, which give R_{n,k}=2(n-k)(k+2theta)/(k(2n-k-1)). Its neighboring difference has a strictly positive denominator times H linear with positive slope in theta. At theta=-1/[2(n-1)], H=n(k-2)(kn-2k+n)/(n-1)>=0 with equality solely at k=2. The k=2 inequality is negative below the threshold, proving sharp necessity. Exact independent rational checks cover 19,764 identities, but the proof is symbolic and infinite.

claim_vs_prior_implication.reasoning: Classical parameter-free coefficient log-concavity neither supplies the theta threshold nor implies weighted log-concavity; the source partition formula identifies the object without settling the inequality. A proof of one cannot be treated as proof of the other.

equivalent_formulations.reasoning: The unweighted Bessel result applies to a factor of the new probability law, not to the weighted law. It cannot imply the claimed nontrivial negative-strength boundary, and the explicit violating example proves why a direct transfer is invalid.

originality.rationale: Comparisons with the fully inspected 2021 partition model and 2004 Bessel log-concavity result show neither implies the strength-weighted sharp threshold: the latter applies only before multiplication by the theta-dependent factor, and an explicit admissible weighted counterexample defeats inference. Related generalized Stirling and two-parameter inference sources were also compared; targeted published searches found no matching result, with residual unindexed-literature risk.
residual_risks: An unindexed treatment of the negative-strength half-discount partition law could contain the same criterion.
Earlier generalized-Stirling results could admit a non-obvious reinterpretation not evident in the compared theorem statements; no such implication was identified.

value.rationale: This is a complete, sharp, infinite-n classification of an intrinsic random partition block-count distribution at the distinguished Brownian/half-discount parameter. It identifies the precise negative-strength sample-size phase transition, equality case, and obstruction by the very first interior inequality, extending beyond known coefficient-only log-concavity.
